claims: NASA's Artemis II mission targets launch as early as April 1, 2026.
Artemis II will send four astronauts on a 10-day trip around the Moon.
Artemis II marks the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years.
Artemis II will send astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen around the Moon.
The primary aim of Artemis II is to test critical life support systems on the Orion spacecraft and the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Artemis I (2022) successfully completed an uncrewed flight test.
Artemis II (2026) is a crewed lunar flyby.
Artemis III is planned as a technological test.
Subsequent landings from 2028 aim for the lunar south pole.
The Artemis missions rely on partnerships with commercial entities for landers.
The Artemis missions have international collaborators including the Canadian Space Agency.
